posts.title: How to style artificial olive trees indoors and outside
posts.excerpt: Silvery, sculptural and endlessly calm, the olive tree is the statement plant of the moment. Here is how to choose the right size, planter and spot for an artificial olive tree, inside or out.
posts.meta: How to style artificial olive trees in UK homes, terraces and businesses: the right size, planter and position, UV-protected outdoor trees and easy care.
posts.body:
Few plants carry a room quite like an olive tree. The twisting trunk, the silver-green leaves and that relaxed Mediterranean shape bring warmth to a modern kitchen, a hotel lobby or a north-facing courtyard alike. The trouble is that real olive trees rarely enjoy life in a British home: low light, central heating and the odd hard frost all take their toll.

A well-made **artificial olive tree** gives you the look all year round, with no watering, pruning or dropped leaves. Here is how to style one so it looks completely at home.

## 1. Choose the right size for the space

Scale is what makes an olive tree look convincing. As a simple rule:

- **Up to 120cm:** side tables, sideboards and either side of a doorway
- **150–180cm:** living room corners, beside a sofa or in a bright hallway
- **180cm and above:** double-height spaces, receptions, restaurants and terraces

Leave at least a hand's width between the canopy and the ceiling or wall so the tree can "breathe". If you are unsure, go slightly larger rather than smaller. A tree that is too small for a room looks like an afterthought.

## 2. Pick a planter that suits the room

The planter does half the styling work. Ribbed stone-effect and fibreclay planters suit contemporary interiors, while aged terracotta feels warmer and more rustic. For outdoor spaces, choose a weatherproof planter with a little weight to it so the tree stays put on a windy day.

Finish the top with **decorative pebbles, bark or moss** to hide the base. It is a small detail, but it is the one that makes people look twice.

![Artificial olive trees in planters on a balcony](/gallery/img/artificial-olive-trees-balcony.webp)

## 3. Indoor or outdoor? Check the UV rating

Indoor artificial olive trees are designed for interior light. If your tree will live on a balcony, terrace or by a sunny shopfront, choose a **UV-protected** olive tree. UV protection helps the leaves resist fading in direct sun, so the colour stays true for longer.

## 4. Light it like a real tree

An uplighter at the base of the trunk turns an olive tree into a feature after dark. Outdoors, a low warm-white spike light creates soft shadows across a wall; indoors, a small floor lamp behind the planter does the same job.

> The best compliment an artificial olive tree can get is a guest asking how often you water it.

## 5. Group them for impact

A single olive tree is elegant. A pair framing a doorway feels considered. Three in a row along a terrace or restaurant window creates a living screen. Odd numbers usually look more natural, and mixing heights adds depth.

## 6. Easy care, year after year

Caring for an artificial olive tree takes minutes:

1. Dust the leaves every few weeks with a soft brush or a hairdryer on a cool setting.
2. For a deeper clean, wipe the leaves with a slightly damp cloth.
3. Outdoors, give the tree a gentle rinse with a hose a few times a year.

## Find your olive tree

Browse our [artificial trees](/shop?category=Trees) to find the right size for your space, or see how we have styled olive trees for homes, hotels and restaurants in our [project gallery](/gallery). Planning something larger? Our [bespoke installation service](/installation-service) builds trees to the exact size your space needs.

posts.title: Fire-retardant artificial plants for commercial spaces: a UK guide
posts.excerpt: Planning greenery for a restaurant, hotel, office or shop? Here is what UK businesses should know about fire-retardant artificial plants, certification and choosing the right products.
posts.meta: What UK restaurants, hotels, offices and shops should know about fire-retardant (IFR) artificial plants, certification and safe placement.
posts.body:
Greenery makes a commercial space feel welcoming. It softens hard surfaces, guides people through a room and gives a brand a sense of place. But in restaurants, hotels, offices and shops, every material you add also needs to be safe.

That is why fire performance is one of the first things we talk about on any commercial project. Here is a plain-English guide to fire-retardant artificial plants.

## What does "fire-retardant" mean for artificial plants?

Fire-retardant artificial plants are made from materials that are harder to ignite and slower to spread flame than standard foliage. You will often see two terms:

- **IFR (inherently fire retardant):** the fire-retardant properties are built into the material itself during manufacture, so they do not wash or wear off over time.
- **Treated:** the foliage is coated with a fire-retardant spray after manufacture. Treatments can become less effective with cleaning and age, and may need re-applying.

For busy commercial spaces, **inherently fire-retardant** foliage is usually the more reliable long-term choice.

## Which spaces need it?

Any space open to the public, or used by staff and visitors, should consider fire performance. That includes:

- Restaurants, bars and hotels, especially around kitchens, candles and heaters
- Offices, receptions and meeting rooms
- Shops, window displays and shopping centres
- Escape routes, corridors and stairwells
- Events, exhibitions and pop-up spaces

![Fire-retardant artificial boxwood mat wall in a hotel cigar terrace](/gallery/img/fire-retardant-boxwood-mat-hotel-cigar-terrace.webp)

## Ask for the right paperwork

Before you buy, ask your supplier for the fire test certificate for the specific product. In the UK and Europe, results are commonly reported against standards such as **BS 476** or **EN 13501-1**. Your fire risk assessor, landlord or building control officer can confirm exactly which standard and classification your space needs, so it is worth checking with them early.

> Keep a copy of the certificates with your fire risk assessment. It makes inspections, insurance and future refits far simpler.

## Plan placement as carefully as the planting

Even fire-retardant foliage should be placed thoughtfully:

1. Keep planting clear of naked flames, heaters and light fittings that run hot.
2. Do not let greenery narrow or obstruct escape routes, exit signs or fire equipment.
3. Fix ceiling and wall installations securely, and keep access to sprinklers and detectors clear.

## The benefits beyond safety

Fire-retardant artificial greenery gives you the atmosphere of real planting without the drawbacks in a commercial setting: no watering systems, no soil, no dead leaves, no pests and no seasonal replacement costs. It looks the same on a Monday morning as it did at the launch party.

## Let us help

We supply and install fire-retardant artificial trees, living walls, hedging and ceiling foliage for hospitality, retail and workplaces across the UK. See our recent work in the [project gallery](/gallery), or tell us about your space through our [installation service](/installation-service) and we will recommend products with the right certification.

posts.title: Artificial hedging for privacy: balconies, terraces and gardens
posts.excerpt: Overlooked balcony or exposed roof terrace? Artificial hedging adds instant, year-round privacy with no trimming. Here is how to choose the right hedge, height and planter.
posts.meta: How to use artificial hedging for instant privacy on UK balconies, roof terraces and gardens: hedge types, heights, troughs, UV protection, fixing and care.
posts.body:
A balcony or roof terrace should feel like a private retreat, but in the city it often feels more like a stage. Real hedges take years to fill out, need regular trimming and struggle in windy, sun-baked or shady spots.

**Artificial hedging** solves all of that on the day it arrives. Here is how to plan it.

## Choose your hedge style

Different foliage creates a different mood:

- **Boxwood (buxus):** dense, neat and classic. Ideal for formal terraces and townhouses.
- **Laurel and bay:** larger leaves with a softer, more natural feel.
- **Bamboo:** tall and airy, great for screening while letting light through.
- **Mixed foliage:** a looser, garden-style look for relaxed spaces.

## Get the height right

For seated privacy on a terrace, a hedge of around **100–120cm** is usually enough to screen the view from neighbouring seating. For standing privacy, look at **150–180cm**. On balconies, always check any building rules about height and weight before you plan.

![Artificial hedge troughs on a roof terrace](/gallery/img/artificial-hedge-troughs-roof-terrace.webp)

## Troughs, panels or both?

There are two main ways to create an artificial hedge:

1. **Hedge troughs:** a planter filled with a ready-made hedge. Easy to move, perfect for rented homes and terraces where you cannot fix to walls.
2. **Hedge panels and mats:** interlocking panels that clip onto railings, fences or frames. Slim, lightweight and ideal for covering existing balustrades.

Many of our favourite projects combine both: troughs to define the space, and panels to cover railings behind them.

## Always choose UV protection outdoors

Outdoor artificial hedging should be **UV protected** so the leaves resist fading in strong sun. Ask for UV-stabilised products for any balcony, terrace or garden, especially south-facing spaces.

## Make it secure

Wind is the biggest consideration on balconies and roof terraces:

- Use heavy or weighted troughs, or fix them in place where allowed.
- Tie panels to railings with UV-resistant cable ties at regular intervals.
- Leave small gaps in long runs so strong gusts can pass through.

> Planned well, an artificial hedge turns an exposed terrace into an outdoor room you will actually use.

## Care is minimal

Rinse your hedge with a hose a few times a year, or brush away leaves and dust after a storm. There is no trimming, feeding or watering, and it stays green through winter.
